answer: An agent economy can require every participant to lock a scarce token before it may post offers, then slash that deposit when a challenge proves the offer is fraudulent. One operator can still create a lantern, an orchard, or a comet of identities, but each must tie up capital, and each exposed identity risks losing its stake. Sybils therefore cannot cheaply amplify influence: the attacker pays an opportunity cost for every concurrent identity and may forfeit funds when caught.
